$comment: VENDORED SNAPSHOT of the C# reference named-flag / quirk / preset / listener inventory, extracted from packet-net/packet.net src/Packet.Core + src/Packet.Ax25. This is the C# side of the pico-node parity contract, checked in so scripts/parity-check.mjs runs on a self-hosted runner with NO cross-repo token. Refresh it when the C# inventory changes — see parity/README.md. Each item is either mapped to an opted-in manifest vector_set (coverage) OR must be listed in parity-exceptions.json with a reason; the checker fails on any item that is neither.

source.plus: packet.net quirk-spec-names branch, which renames quirkFlags.UnexpectedUaIgnored to Ax25Spec114UnexpectedUaIgnored, quirkFlags.RepeatedConnectUaIgnored to Ax25Spec114RepeatedConnectUaIgnored (both packethacking/ax25spec#114, removal tracked in packet-net/packet.net#880), and quirkFlags.RepeatedConnectSabmReacknowledged to Ax25Spec50RepeatedConnectSabmReacknowledged (packethacking/ax25spec#50, removal tracked in packet-net/packet.net#881) on top of that commit
source.extraction: regex-over-source, mirroring ax25-ts scripts/parity-check.mjs: `public bool X { get;` flags, `public static <Type> X { get;` presets, `public T X { get;` listener options within the Ax25ListenerOptions class body, `public (async)? T X(` methods + `public event T X;` events within the Ax25Listener class body.

coverageLegend.coverage: { set: <manifest vector_set name>, capability?: <capability that set must declare> } — the item is covered iff that set is in=true (and, when a capability is named, that set declares it).
coverageLegend.unmapped: an item with no `coverage` MUST appear in parity-exceptions.json (inventoryExceptions[section][name]) with a reason, or the checker fails.

items.name: SrejCommandIgnored
items.note: Ignore the retransmit request in an SREJ sent as a COMMAND (§4.3.2.4 makes SREJ response-only; direwolf and linbpq both refuse), while still processing its N(R) ack. Became a named flag when the corrected figc4.5 (ax25sdl 0.10.1) made the command paths actionable — packet-net/packet.net#674.

items.name: Ax25Spec114RepeatedConnectUaIgnored
items.note: Drop a byte-identical repeat of the UA that just connected a dial (duplicate delivery, e.g. LinBPQ with two AXIP MAP lines for one address) instead of figc4.4's unexpected-UA reset - packet-net/packet.net#842, renamed from RepeatedConnectUaIgnored per packethacking/ax25spec#114 (removal tracked in packet-net/packet.net#880). Not yet mirrored here: excepted in parity-exceptions.json, tracked in #95.

items.name: Ax25Spec114UnexpectedUaIgnored
items.note: Drop any UA received while the link is up (Connected or Timer Recovery) instead of figc4.4/figc4.5's unexpected-UA reset, as LinBPQ and the Linux kernel do - packet-net/packet.net#874, renamed from UnexpectedUaIgnored per packethacking/ax25spec#114 (removal tracked in packet-net/packet.net#880). Not yet mirrored here: excepted in parity-exceptions.json; no tracking issue opened yet.

items.name: Ax25Spec50RepeatedConnectSabmReacknowledged
items.note: Answer a byte-identical repeat of the peer's connecting SABM(E) (it lost our UA and retried) with UA again instead of figc4.4/figc4.5's reset, which discards the I-frame queue - packet-net/packet.net#856, renamed from RepeatedConnectSabmReacknowledged per packethacking/ax25spec#50 (removal tracked in packet-net/packet.net#881). Not yet mirrored here: excepted in parity-exceptions.json, tracked in #97.
